The direct method involves calculating the sum of the products of each class mark and its frequency, then dividing by the total frequency. The assumed mean method and step-deviation method are simplified forms of the direct method that involve subtracting an assumed mean from each class mark and then adjusting the frequencies accordingly.

The mode of grouped data is the value inside the modal class, which can be found using the formula: Mode = l + (f1 - f0) / (2f1 - f0 - f2) * h, where l is the lower limit of the modal class, h is the class size, f1 is the frequency of the modal class, f0 is the frequency of the class preceding the modal class, and f2 is the frequency of the class succeeding the modal class.

metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Mode of Grouped Data in Grade 10 Mathematics.

Median of Grouped Data

Key terms: median, grouped data, median class, cumulative frequency

To find the median of grouped data, first determine the median class (the class with a cumulative frequency greater than and closest to n/2), then use the formula: Median = l + (cf - n/2) / f * h, where l is the lower limit of the median class, n is the total number of observations, cf is the cumulative frequency of the class preceding the median class, f is the frequency of the median class, and h is the class size.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Mathematics | Calculate Median Height
text:
Calculate Median Height

Key terms: Median, Class Intervals, Cumulative Frequency

To find the median height, first calculate the class intervals and their frequencies. Then use the formula: Median = l + (cf - 0.5n) / f * h, where l is the lower limit, cf is the cumulative frequency of the class preceding the median class, n is the total number of observations, h is the class size, and f is the frequency of the median class.

Key terms: Median, Data Set, Ordering

The median is the middle value in a data set when the data is ordered from least to greatest. If there is an even number of observations, the median is the average of the two middle numbers.

The mean is the most frequently used measure of central tendency, but it can be affected by extreme values. The median is more appropriate when individual observations are not important, and the mode is best for establishing the most frequent value.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Mathematics | Probability Definition
text:
Probability Definition

Key terms: probability, favorable outcomes, possible outcomes

Probability is the likelihood of an event occurring, calculated as the ratio of favorable outcomes to the total possible outcomes, assuming equally likely outcomes.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Mathematics | Impossible and Sure Events
text:
Impossible and Sure Events

Key terms: impossible event, sure event, complement

An impossible event has a probability of 0, while a sure event has a probability of 1. The probability of an event and its complement always sum up to 1.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Impossible and Sure Events in Grade 10 Mathematics.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Mathematics | Complementary Events
text:
Complementary Events

Key terms: complementary events, mutually exclusive, probability of complement

Complementary events are mutually exclusive events whose probabilities sum up to 1. The probability of an event and its complement are equal to 1.

title: NCERT Grade 10 Mathematics | Probability Range
text:
Probability Range

Key terms: probability range, favorable outcomes, possible outcomes

The probability of an event is always between 0 and 1, inclusive. This is because the number of favorable outcomes is always less than or equal to the total possible outcomes.
